3. As per the prosecution story, complainant Smt. Laxmi Bai made a complaint before the P.S. Aerodrome, Indore by stating that she along with her husband are working in a farm house, which was owned by the appellant Sunil Karosiya.

Before one month from the date of incident appellant Sunil Karosiya asked the complainant Laxmi Bai to send her daughter (prosecutrix) for doing household work and offerred salary of Rs.500/- per month.
Thereafter complainant send the prosecutrix to a Flat situated at Ramkamal Residency near Gomatgiri, Indore, which was owned by appellant Pinki @ Sarita.

On 30.5.2013 prosecutrix communicated to her mother Laxmi Bai that both the appellants sexually exploited her and appellant Sunil committed forcefully rape repeatedly with the help of co-accused Pinki and appellant Sunil also caused injury to the prosecutrix by knife on left ankle and both the appellants did not allow the complainant and her husband to meet the prosecutrix.
Accordingly offence has been registered.

4. The case of the prosecution is further that Dr. P.S. Tripathi (PW-9) examined the prosecutrix regarding determination of her age and on the basis of her x-ray report,
he opined that age of the prosecutrix is between 12 to 14 years.

Dr. Poonam Mathur (PW-7) along with the team of doctors examined the prosecutrix and opined that her hymen was old torn and sign of old scratch has been found on the left ankle, she appears to be habitual for sexual intercourse.
Her slide of vaginal swab has been prepared and also seized her pubic hair along with her underwear.
Accused Sunil has been arrested and on the basis of his discovery statement, a knife and a car has been recovered from his possession and he was sent for medical examination.
Slide of his semen was also prepared.
All the seized articles were sent to the FSL for its chemical examination.
5. After completion of the investigation, charge sheet has been filed before the Special Judge (POCSO Act).
Prosecution has examined as many as 19 witnesses, while the defence has examined 4 witnesses.
Trial court after scrutinizing the entire evidence available on record, convicted and sentenced both the appellants as mentioned hereinabove.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment of conviction, both the appellants have preferred these two separate appeals.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant Pinki has preferred Criminal Appeal No.1249/2014 by stating that the impugned judgment passed by the trial Court is bad in law.
She has been maliciously confined for the aforesaid offence.
The sole testimony of the prosecutrix is not supported by any other eyewitness and medical evidence.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the statement of the prosecution witnesses.
The trial court has committed error in not considering the defence of the appellant.
All the witnesses are interested witnesses.
No independent witness has been examined by the prosecution.

Hence, he prays that the impugned judgment be set aside and Pinki @ Sarita D/O Hardayal Singh ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5645462/

sentences.text: Appellant Sunil Karosiya has preferred Criminal Appeal No.1273/2014 by stating that the entire story of the prosecution appears to be imaginary and hypothetical.
There is inordinate delay in lodging the FIR.
FIR is an afterthought and coloured with malafide intention.
There are material contradictions and omissions in the statements of the prosecutrix and other witnesses.
Medical evidence does not corroborate the statement of the prosecutrix.
Irregularity has been committed in respect of the collection of blood and semen of the present appellant.
Prosecutrix never complained or informed about the alleged offence to anyone.
The FIR was lodged only to extort money from the appellant.
Hence, he prays that the impugned judgment be set aside and the appellant be acquitted from all the charges.
8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/State submitted that the impugned judgment passed by the trial Court is based upon cogent evidence and proper appreciation of evidence.
Trial court has rightly convicted and sentenced both the appellants and the same does not call for any interference.
9. Learned counsel for both the parties heard at length and perused the entire record.
10. The question which arises for consideration of this Court is firstly, whether the prosecutrix, at the time of incident, was minor?
11. Prosecutrix (PW-2) categorically stated that her age is about 10 years.
During the cross-examination of the prosecutrix, both the appellants did not challenge factum of her age.

Dr.
P.S. Tripathi (PW-9) who has conducted the ossification test of the prosecutrix, categorically stated that as per the ossification test the age of the prosecutrix has been found between 12 to 14 years and his report is Ex.P/7.
No specific challenge to the ossification test (Ex.P/7) has been made by the defence and no other evidence in rebuttal has been filed.
Therefore, on the basis of the aforesaid evidence, it is proved that prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident.

12. So far as the sexual assault is concerned, prosecutrix (PW-2) categorically stated in her statement that appellant Sunil has committed forcefully rape upon her and compelled her for licking his penis.
Appellant Sunil also caused injury to her by knife on her left ankle.

Dr. Anubha (PW-5)
who has conducted the MLC of the prosecutrix, categorically stated that her hymen was found old torn but no swelling or bleeding and redness was found on her private part at the time of examination.
One finger was easily entered in her vagina and no definite opinion regarding recent rape could be given.
She has prepared the slide of her vaginal discharge.

Dr. Poonam Mathur (PW-7)
and Dr. Sumitra Yadav (PW-8) both of them opined that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape and multiple abrasions have been found.

The MLC report is Ex.P/4 & P/5 and query report is Ex.P/7.
13.

Learned counsel for the appellant Sunil contended that in the vaginal slide of the prosecutrix no semen of appellant Sunil was found and no symptom of recent rape has been found in the medical examination of the prosecutrix, therefore, case under Section 376 of IPC is not made out against the appellant, but in the instant case the hymen of the prosecutrix was found torn and as per the Pinki @ Sarita D/O Hardayal Singh ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5645462/

16. The evidence of the prosecutrix (PW-2) is well corroborated by her mother Laxmibai (PW-18),
coordinator of the Child Line Manisha (PW-1) & Wasim Iqbal (PW-3), who have deposed in their statement that prosecutrix has narrated before them that she was subjected to rape by the appellant Sunil.

They also corroborated that co-accused Pinki had also forced the prosecutrix to do some acts,
which may be considered in terms of unnatural sex.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants contended that the place of occurrence is situated in the densely populated locality and it is not possible that such offence can be committed by the appellants at that place.
The incident has taken place in the house of the deceased- appellant Pinki, where the prosecutrix was working as a domestic servant.
Prosecutrix categorically stated that accused persons done such obscene and sexual act in the dark of the night in absence of other persons.
At the time of commission of the act, the chances of the resistance or raising an alarm depends upon various factors.
In the instant case, it is stated that appellant Sunil had attacked upon the prosecutrix by knife and she has sustained injury and entire incident had taken place at the night time.
Therefore, in such circumstances, when no resistance has occurred, it does not mean that the act was not possible in densely populated area.

18. Another submission made by learned counsel for the appellants is that no internal or external injuries are found on the person of the prosecutrix, therefore, in absence of the medical corroboration her sole statement cannot be relied upon.

In this regard, this Court can rely upon the judgment in the case of Bharwada Bhoginbhai Hirjibhai Vs. State of Gujarat reported in AIR 1993 SC 753, in which it has been held that:-
"Corroboration is not the sine-quo-non for a conviction in a rape case.

entities.text: Bharwada Bhoginbhai Hirjibhai Vs. State of Gujarat reported in AIR 1993 SC 753
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the Indian setting, refusal to act on the testimony of a victim of sexual assault in the absence of corroboration as a rule, is adding insult to injury.

Viewing the evidence of the girl or the women who complains of rape or sexual molestation with the aid of spectacles fitted with lenses tinged with doubt, disbelief or suspicion, is to justify the charge of male chauvinism in a male dominated society."
"On principle the evidence of a victim of sexual assault stands on par with evidence of an injured witness.

Just as a witness who has sustained an injury (which is not shown or believed to be self- inflicted) is the best witness in the sense that he is least likely to exculpate the real offender, the evidence of a victim of a sex- offence is entitled to great weight, absence of corroboration notwithstanding."

19. Learned counsel for the appellants further contended that the prosecutrix is a minor child and she has been tutored by her mother and officials of the Child Care, there are material contradictions and omissions in her statement, therefore, her statement cannot be relied upon.
Although in the instant case prosecutrix is a minor girl, but her examination has been done before the trial Court in the question-answer form and she has confidently answered all the questions.

Although some contradictions and omissions are found in her statement, but such contradictions and omissions are trivial in nature and same are neither material nor sufficient to disbelieve her testimony, which is corroborated by other witnesses.
Prosecutrix and her mother have no motive to falsely implicate the appellants in the instant case.

It is the settled position of law that conviction can be based on evidence of solitary eyewitness and omissions or lapses in investigation cannot be a ground to discard the prosecution case, which is otherwise creditable and cogent.
Ocular testimony of the eyewitness cannot be discarded lightly.

(See: State of M.P. Vs. Chakkilal and Another and Ramveer Pinki @ Sarita D/O Hardayal Singh ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5645462/
6 Vs. Chakkilal and Another reported in 2018(4) Crimes 238 SC).

sentences.text: It must not be overlooked that a minor innocent girl was subjected to sexual assault, is not accomplice to a crime, but is a victim of another person's lust and it is improper and undesirable to test her evidence with a certain amount of suspicion, treating her as if she was an accomplice.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Mahendra @ Golu reported in AIR 2021 SC 5242 has held that:-
"21.

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Mahendra @ Golu reported in AIR 2021 SC 5242
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is overwhelming evidence on record to prove the respondent's deliberate overt steps to take the minor girls inside his house; closing the door(s); undressing the victims and rubbing his genitals on those of the prosecutrices.
As the victims started crying, the respondent could not succeed in his penultimate act and there was a sheer providential escape from actual penetration.
Had the respondent succeeded in penetration, even partially, his act would have fallen within the contours of `Rape' as it stood conservatively defined under Section 375 IPC at that time.
22. The deposition by the victims (PW-1 and PW-2) are impeccable.
Both have unequivocally stated as to how the respondent allured them and indulged in all those traumatic acts which have already been narrated in the preceding paragraphs.

The statements of both the victim-children inspire full confidence, establish their innocence and evince a natural version without any remote possibility of tutoring."
21.

Although in the vaginal swab of the prosecutrix no semen or spermatozoa of the appellant Sunil has been found as per the report Ex.P/31, but on the seized Pyjama of the prosecutrix semen of the appellant Sunil has been found as proved by the DNA Profile report (Ex.P/31).
Therefore, it is also a strong evidence against the appellant.
22. There is a overwhelming evidence on record to prove the case of the prosecution.
The deposition of the prosecutrix is impeachable.
She has unequivocally stated as to how both the appellants allured her and indulged in all these traumatic acts, which has been already narrated in the preceding paragraphs.
The statement of the prosecutrix inspire full confidence, establishes her innocence and evince a natural version without any remote possibility of tutoring.
Her statement is well supported by medical evidence as well as DNA Profile report (Ex.P/31).

Applying the well settled principles of law, as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, as aforesaid, to the facts of the case, it is evident that the crime of rape after confining the child victim in the house of the appellant Pinki, was committed by the appellant Sunil with the help of co-accused Pinki.

23. After appreciating the entire evidence available on record, we are of the considered view that there is no material available on record for warranting any interference in the findings recorded by the trial Court.
Therefore, the finding of conviction and sentence recorded by the trial Court is just and proper.
Being devoid of any merits, both these appeals deserve to be and are hereby dismissed.
24. Let a copy of this judgment along with the record of the trial Court be sent to the concerned trial Court for information and necessary compliance.

Applying the well settled principles of law, as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, as aforesaid, to the facts of the case, it is evident that the crime of rape after confining the child victim in the house of the appellant Pinki, was committed by the appellant Sunil with the help of co-accused Pinki.
23. After appreciating the entire evidence available on record, we are of the considered view that there is no material available on record for warranting any interference in the findings recorded by the trial Court.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the finding of conviction and sentence recorded by the trial Court is just and proper.
Being devoid of any merits, both these appeals deserve to be and are hereby dismissed.
24. Let a copy of this judgment along with the record of the trial Court be sent to the concerned trial Court for information and necessary compliance.
